scope: Bound typed DXF output for embedded LTYPE group-9 text after the configured DXF encoding and text escaping, while retaining tolerant input and atomic record failure.

implementationReadiness.sourceObservation: dxfRW::writeLineType emitted complex-dash group 9 through writeUtf8String without checking the final encoded value length. ASCII DXF escapes selected control bytes, legacy DXF converts UTF-8 through the configured code page, and R2007+ DXF emits UTF-8.

normativeEvidence.relevantRule: The exact group-code range 1-4, 7, 9, 300-309 has a 255-character maximum, less for Unicode strings.

normativeEvidence.source: Autodesk 2024 Group Code Value Types Reference (DXF)
normativeEvidence.relevantRule: The group-code range 0-9 has a 2049-single-byte-character allowance after the introduction of extended symbol names in AutoCAD 2000; UTF-8 is used for AutoCAD 2007 and later.
Group 9 carries the text string for each embedded-text linetype element; the page gives no independent length limit.

implementationReadiness.sourceConflict: The direct-field ObjectARX table gives group 9 a 255-character maximum; the 2024 group-range table gives 0-9 a 2049-single-byte-character allowance starting with AutoCAD 2000. Neither page adjudicates this discrepancy for native LTYPE consumers. The implementation uses a conservative 255 encoded-byte output admission bound across target versions until producer/native evidence qualifies a larger profile.
implementationReadiness.change: Added dxfWriter::writeUtf8StringBounded, which checks the UTF-8/code-page and ASCII-control-escaped value before writing. Typed LTYPE output applies a 255-byte group-9 bound. The parser remains unchanged and tolerant of longer source values. Over-limit output fails within DxfWriterRecordScope and does not publish a partial LTYPE record.

profiles: AC1012/AC1015 legacy code-page ASCII and Binary DXF
AC1021 UTF-8 ASCII and Binary DXF
coverage: 255 encoded bytes are admitted and typed readback preserves the text; 256 bytes are atomically refused across the selected DXF versions and both encodings.
Legacy ANSI_1252 and modern UTF-8 multibyte boundaries are measured after conversion; selected Unicode values round-trip through typed LTYPE parsing.
ASCII caret control escaping is included in the encoded-byte limit; Binary DXF does not use the ASCII caret escaping path.
A refused staged record leaves the output empty and restores writer error state; the same writer successfully commits a corrected record.

limitations: The 255-byte bound is a conservative typed-writer policy under conflicting Autodesk references; it does not prove the format-wide maximum or justify a support claim for either short or long LTYPE text.
No independent producer, AutoCAD, LibreCAD, LibreCAD_3, or FreeCAD native acceptance test was run for the group-9 size boundary.
Read-side admission, LTYPE group-9 strings longer than 255 bytes, and version-specific native acceptance remain unqualified. No DWG behavior was changed.
nextReadyPacket: Continue P6 with the remaining LTYPE unit/inheritance profiles; keep the group-9 larger-string limit open until eligible producer/native evidence resolves the Autodesk reference conflict.
